rules.source: Personal Data Protection Act 2010 (Act 709), significantly amended 2024 (Act A1727). Regulator: Department of Personal Data Protection (JPDP), official site https://www.pdp.gov.my/ppdpv1/en/main-page/ , official Act text https://www.pdp.gov.my/ppdpv1/en/akta/pdp-act-2010-en/
rules.retrieved_snippet: Governs processing of personal data in commercial transactions, built on seven principles (General, Notice and Choice, Disclosure, Security, Retention, Data Integrity, Access). The 2024 amendment added mandatory breach notification, DPO appointment requirements, direct obligations on data processors, and expanded sensitive-data definitions to include biometric data; penalties raised to RM 1 million and/or 3 years imprisonment.

rules.source: Online Safety Act 2025 and its Child Protection Code (CPC), in force 1 June 2026, enforced by MCMC; also Communications and Multimedia (Amendment) Act 2025, Child Act 2001, and Sexual Offences against Children Act 2017. Summary: https://xident.io/blog/malaysia-under-16-social-media-ban-child-protection-code-compliance-2026/
rules.retrieved_snippet: Malaysia is one of the first countries worldwide, and the second in Asia, to enforce a minimum social-media age. The CPC requires age verification against government-issued records for platforms likely accessed by children (minimum age 16), applying to licensed social media providers with 8M+ Malaysian users (MCMC names Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube specifically). The Online Safety Act/Amendment Act also classify CSAM as priority harmful content.

rules.source: Consumer Protection Act 1999 (Act 599), Royal Assent 27 August 1999, gazetted 9 September 1999, last major amendment 23 July 2019 (Tribunal for Consumer Claims). Regulator: Ministry of Domestic Trade and Cost of Living (KPDN), official Act text https://www.kpdn.gov.my/images/2024/awam/akta/ttpm/Act%20599.pdf
rules.retrieved_snippet: Malaysia's principal consumer protection statute, amended over time to cover unfair contract terms and establish the Tribunal for Consumer Claims for expedited dispute resolution.

rules.source: Computer Crimes Act 1997 (Act 563), s.3 unauthorised access to computer material; Cybercrimes Bill 2026 would repeal and replace it — https://www.rahmatlim.com/publication/articles/33327/cybercrimes-bill-2026-closing-the-gaps-in-malaysia-s-cybercrime-legal-framework (status page); s.3 text via search of https://asianlaws.org/gcld/cyberlawdb/MY/Computer%20Crimes%20Act%201997.pdf
rules.retrieved_snippet: Section 3 of the Computer Crimes Act 1997 makes it an offence to cause a computer to perform any function with intent to secure unauthorised access to any program or data, knowing the access is unauthorised. Rahmat Lim: the Cybercrimes Bill 2026 would repeal the CCA; 'On 20 July 2026, the Dewan Negara passed the Cybercrimes Bill 2026' — royal assent and commencement not stated in the article, so the CCA is treated as the operative law here; re-verify.

rules.source: Communications and Multimedia Act 1998 (Act 588), improper use of network facilities or services (s.233 per MCMC/AGC reprint listings; one MCMC listing numbers differently — verify) — https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/LOM/EN/Act%20588.pdf and https://www.mcmc.gov.my/ms/faqs/online-content-problems-2024/2-what-is-mcmc-s-jurisdiction-in-addressing-compla
rules.retrieved_snippet: Search-result summary of MCMC/AGC pages (pages themselves not fetched): s.233 covers knowingly using network or application services to create, solicit or send obscene, indecent, false, menacing or offensive content with intent to annoy, abuse, threaten or harass; conviction carries a fine up to RM50,000, up to one year's imprisonment, or both, plus RM1,000 per continuing day.
